title: Can humans start an earthquake?
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss whether human activity can trigger earthquakes, focusing on reservoir-induced seismicity (RIS) caused by dams, linked to the May 2008 Sichuan earthquake near the Zipingpu Dam on the Min Jiang River. They cover how reservoir weight and water seepage into fault cracks (pore pressure) can destabilize faults, the 1963 Vajont Dam landslide and wave in Italy, a 2007 landslide at the Three Gorges Dam that buried a bus, a World Bank survey of dam geology, the 1967 Koyna India quake, wastewater injection, oil and gas extraction and injection, and the Taipei tower. They note dams need conditions such as a fault line and height (around 100 meters) to trigger quakes. The episode ends with announcements about New York meet-and-greet and trivia events, a T-shirt contest, a Guatemala textbook donation drive, and listener mail.

segments.title: Opening sponsor read and banter
segments.summary: Opening sponsor read for GoToMeeting, then Josh and Chuck banter about the show's name and introduce the Sichuan earthquake topic.

segments.title: Introduction to reservoir induced seismicity
segments.summary: The hosts introduce reservoir induced seismicity as a possible man-made cause of the 2008 Sichuan earthquake, and decide to start with dams.

segments.title: How dams change landscapes and cause landslides
segments.summary: Dams alter river hydrology and flood land around reservoirs, sometimes submerging towns such as beneath Lake Lanier. Added water weight can trigger landslides; the Hoover Dam is mentioned.

segments.title: Vajont Dam landslide and Three Gorges landslides
segments.summary: The 1963 Vajont Dam disaster in northern Italy, where rock fell into the reservoir creating a wave over the dam and destroying a village, is described. Landslides at the Three Gorges Dam, including one in 2007 that buried a bus, are also mentioned.

segments.title: Dam-triggered quakes, faults and pore pressure
segments.summary: The Zipingpu Dam's weight and possible fault lines beneath it are discussed, along with a World Bank survey finding unexpected geology at many dam projects. The hosts explain how water seeping into fault cracks raises pore pressure and lubricates faults, and how injecting or extracting fluids can change stresses.

segments.title: Oil, gas, wastewater injection and other man-made quakes
segments.summary: The hosts discuss whether removing oil harms the earth, water and gas injection causing tremors, Colorado quakes in the 1990s linked to gas drilling, and wastewater injection. They mention the 1967 Koyna quake in India and the Taipei tower.

segments.title: Limits on dam-triggered earthquakes
segments.summary: Dams cannot trigger quakes alone; they need factors such as a fault line and a height of roughly 100 meters. The hosts say they are not against dams.

segments.title: Announcements: New York events and T-shirts
segments.summary: Announcements of a New York meet-and-greet at the Knitting Factory, a trivia night at the Bell House, the T-shirt contest, and a Guatemala textbook text donation drive.

segments.title: Listener mail and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts close with the listener mail address and a brief sign-off.
